institutionName: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose my study destination based on the course catalogue, since the institution had courses that weren't offered at UCPH

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Unfortunately 2/3 courses that I wanted were not offered in the spring semester. That was a disappointment and it was not something you could see in the course catalogue

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to find necessary information upon arrival. The host institution did a great job hosting info-meetings and sending the needed information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A orientation meeting two days before first day of class

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot of time finding a place to stay. I used a local facebook group. The most difficult was that leases were for 11 months at a time and started in the fall semester.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I found that it was nice to stay off campus since I had my own space. But a lot of the other exchange students stayed on campus, so you could be left out a bit

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not find the registration process easy at all, especially since you could not rely on the course catalogue for what was offered in the spring semester. You only found out what courses were offered if you could add it in the registration process. That was very late in the process, when you take into account at that point I had been in-process about the exchange for more than a year.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was a bit difficult to understand. Students would gain access at different timeslots and then it's first come first serve. The course catalogue did not have information about when courses is offered, so that was something you found out in the registration process. Exchange students gained access to registration as the last group, which could mean some courses could be full. I luckily did not have issues with dad

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot, but a Zoom-meeting was set up to teach us about the process

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 2 out of 3 classes that I wanted were not offered. I found substitutes were I succeeded in registrering for all of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reach out to the course responsible to find substitutes for courses. And please be aware that the course catalogue is all courses available and they're not offered in every semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level of courses to be lower than at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH I'm used to a lot of lectures, reading material, assignments, presentations, lab work etc. I'm used to "filling" out the course block with full schedule. At my host institution I only had 2,5 hours of lectures every week in each course. I had not a lot of reading material, so overall not a lot to do.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ENVR 500
ENVR 775
PHRS 703
CHEM 445

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed ENVR 775 as it was a course about climate change. It focuses not only on the science part, but also on the communication etc. Every week a new lecturer was presented and they were all very good. Even though they were different lectures through out the course there was a nice coherence between lectures.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of different clubs for students. Being in the US the college sport is a must to experience. It is free for students and it gives a great sense of belonging to the institution.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend seing as much sport as possible. Is fun to experience

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I visited Washington DC, Nashville (very fun), Asheville (and surrounding mountains), a roadtrip down the east coast ending in Miami). I highly recommend visiting the surrounding states.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult as most of my social circle consisted of exchange students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was very difficult to become friends with local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it challenging that the society is build around owning a car

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The college culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) the courses will work out and do not stress it
2) the living situation will also work out in the end 
3) do not stress the social life

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be open for everything and you'll have a great experience

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social part

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from friends and family

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
